short_title: Is your hand dryer blowing germs on you? 😳 #shorts
short_description:
Team towel or team dryer? Here's what the science says.

Hot-air hand dryers pull in restroom air and can blow its bacteria onto your hands (University of Connecticut, Applied and Environmental Microbiology, 2018; HEPA filters cut that by about four times). Near jet dryers, a University of Leeds study (Journal of Hospital Infection, 2014) found about 27 times more airborne germs than near paper towel dispensers, but that study was funded by the paper industry, and other studies found smaller differences.

The CDC says either a clean towel or a hand dryer works. The rule that really matters: dry your hands completely, because germs transfer more easily to and from wet hands.

Team towel or team dryer? Comment below 👇

More everyday habits: https://youtube.com/shorts/_WgIPvYNgzY

Sources: University of Connecticut (2018), University of Leeds (2014), CDC handwashing guidance.
